definition: A phase of matter with no fixed shape or volume, whose particles are far apart and move fast and randomly, with negligible forces between them except during collisions.
The mass per unit volume of a substance, $\rho = \frac{m}{V}$, measured in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
A measure of the average random kinetic energy of the particles of a substance; thermal energy flows from higher to lower temperature.

The absolute temperature scale, with zero at absolute zero and steps the same size as degrees Celsius, so $T$ in K is the Celsius temperature plus 273; use it in every equation that multiplies or divides by temperature.

The constant $k_\text{B} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{J K}^{-1}$ linking absolute temperature to the average kinetic energy of one particle; it is per particle, unlike the gas constant $R$, which is per mole.
